questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: For me it was important to choose a destination where the mother language was english to make it more easy to socialize with locals.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The main reason for the high rating is overall Canada as a country. Nice culture, beautiful places and very welcoming. In addition, I had interesting courses.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very difficult. I spent a lot of time mailing with the host university.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: They offered introduction events and a get together week before the studies start (But is also for first year students at the university, so I would not recommend joining).

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Keele and Glendon campus. I would not recommend statying on campus unless you stay at Glendon. Keele is to big and it is difficult find other exchange students.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Meal plans are mandatory and the food is in general not really good but just expensive

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Glendon is nice, but not Keele. Campus experience is fun, but one semester is more than enough. On the other hand it is very difficult to find housing in downtown and moreover it is more expensive than living on campus.

questions.answer: Very different, it was a bit more like high school. Participation grades, a lot of smaller assignment. Your grade is not just your final exam.
